req.title: Login form GET
req.statement: The system shall serve a login form at GET /auth/login.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-007 requires GET /auth/login to return an HTTP 2xx response with a login form payload. Three tests are designed: (1) a positive EP test verifying exact status 200 and presence of key HTML form elements (catches status-code mutations and content mutations); (2) a negative NEG test verifying that an unsupported method (POST with no data) still returns a valid response but that a wrong method like DELETE returns 405, distinguishing the GET handler from other methods; (3) a BVA boundary test verifying the response Content-Type header and that the response body contains both 'username' and 'password' input fields, catching mutations that alter the template rendering path. Each test is self-contained, uses in-process Flask test client, and asserts exact values to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

def test_login_get_returns_200_with_form():
    r = client.get('/auth/login')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'username' in r.data
    assert b'password' in r.data
    assert b'<form' in r.data
    assert b'Log In' in r.data or b'login' in r.data.lower()

test_login_get_returns_200_with_form()

tests.name: test_login_get_not_redirect_and_not_5xx
preconditions: Flask app is created with TESTING=True and a temporary database
actions: Send GET /auth/login and verify it is not a redirect (3xx) and not a server error (5xx)
Send DELETE /auth/login and verify it returns 405 Method Not Allowed
expected: GET /auth/login status code is exactly 200, not 301, 302, 404, or 500
trace: R-FLASKR-007: error pathways — HTTP 4xx on client error; HTTP 5xx on server error
R-FLASKR-007: GET must not redirect anonymous users away from the login page
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

def test_login_get_not_redirect_and_not_5xx():
    r = client.get('/auth/login')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.status_code != 301
    assert r.status_code != 302
    assert r.status_code != 404
    assert r.status_code != 500
    r_del = client.delete('/auth/login')
    assert r_del.status_code == 405

test_login_get_not_redirect_and_not_5xx()

tests.name: test_login_get_content_type_and_form_fields
preconditions: Flask app is created with TESTING=True and a temporary database
actions: Verify both 'name="username"' and 'name="password"' attributes exist in the response body
Verify the form method is POST (boundary: the GET page must render a POST form)
expected: Response body contains method="post" or method="POST" indicating the form submits via POST
trace: R-FLASKR-007: expected payload must include a login form with username and password fields
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

def test_login_get_content_type_and_form_fields():
    r = client.get('/auth/login')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    ct = r.headers.get('Content-Type', '')
    assert ct.startswith('text/html')
    body = r.data
    assert b'name="username"' in body
    assert b'name="password"' in body
    body_lower = body.lower()
    assert b'method="post"' in body_lower or b"method='post'" in body_lower

test_login_get_content_type_and_form_fields()
